key: Then spoke Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel: ‘Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; And thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon.’
s: Joshua speaks as Israel routs five kings, later killed, as are all souls in the cities taken; Rashi, on Joshua 10:12, reads it as silencing the sun’s song, and so its motion, Joshua singing instead, and by the plain sense as bidding it wait.

evidence.words: אָז יְדַבֵּר אָמַר שִׁירָה תַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ דּוֹם, דּוֹם מִלּוֹמַר שִׁירָה, וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֵם, עוֹמֵד וְאֵינוֹ מְהַלֵּךְ, שֶׁבְּכָל עֵת הִילּוּכוֹ הוּא אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה. וּפְשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁל מִקְרָא: דּוֹם לְשׁוֹן הַמְתָּנָה
evidence.gloss: On “Then spoke”: he said a song in place of the sun, because he said to the sun “dom”: be silent from saying song; and all the while it is silent it stands and does not move, for at every moment of its going it says song. And the plain sense of the verse: “dom” is a word for waiting.

reason: verse.js ok, ref Joshua 10:12 and at [196,12] match. Plain sense faithful to Joshua 10: Israel routs the five Amorite kings who besieged Gibeon (10:5 to 11), the kings are later killed and hanged (10:26), and the cities taken are destroyed with all the souls in them (10:28 to 39); the hard clause is plain, no four-word run from the verse. Read the Joshua 10 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on Joshua). Rashi on אז ידבר says Joshua said a song in place of the sun, having told the sun dom, be silent from its song, and while silent it stands still since it sings in every moment of its motion; then gives the plain sense, dom as waiting. The sentence follows this in order and adds nothing; Radak and Metzudat David take dom as waiting only, which is Rashi’s second, plain reading.
